title: Are dental recall intervals risk-based? A cross-sectional study of records in a practice-based research network
subtitle: The design is the investigator's choice: cross-sectional record study or two-year cohort
statement: National guidance asks for recall intervals set between 3 and 24 months by each patient's risk, but in the network's 14 practices most adults appear to be recalled every six months and risk fields are often blank or copied forward. Commissioners want to know whether risk-based recall happens before contracts change in 2028. Two designs are possible: a cross-sectional record study of how intervals are set now, or a two-year cohort of decay by interval; the resources favour the first but the choice is the investigator's.
whoAffected: Adults registered with the 14 practices, especially those in deprived areas; dentists and practice managers; commissioners.
whatHurts: High-risk patients who may be seen too rarely, low-risk patients using appointments they do not need, and access lost for people waiting to register.
currentPractice: Mostly six-month recall with a risk field that is often blank or copied forward.
whyNow: Contract changes are planned for 2028 and the commissioners want a baseline.
constraints: Six months of a part-time research dentist (two days a week) from February 2027; no payments to practices for follow-up data; records only, with no patient contact.
patientCenteredGoal: Each patient is recalled at an interval that matches their risk and is told why.
summary: Problem framed; the family is left for the investigator to choose between two designs.
